# Game rules and logic contract

Reference for the game rules, their defaults, the listener -> logic contract and the backend API
the UI uses. Verified against the code in `app/src/main/java/com/codejam/taptation/logic/`,
`service/CatchFeedback.kt`, `ai/JudgeQueue.kt` and `TaptationApplication.kt`. When this file and
the code disagree, the code wins. Product background: [revised catch flow](../revised-catch-flow.md);
UI boundary: [UI <-> backend contract](../ui-backend-contract.md).

"Bait" means a notification classified as distracting, not a notification generated by this app.

## Rules

| Rule | Behaviour (code default) |
|---|---|
| Health | Starts at 100, clamped to 0-100 |
| Difficulty (`Difficulty`) | Easy 0.20, Medium 0.40, Hard 0.70; Easy selected initially. Only used for a "Let us decide" Bait verdict |
| Catch level (`CatchLevel`) | Mild 10, Medium 20, Savage 10 health damage; Mild selected initially. Each value must be 1-100 |
| Per-app rule (`AppRule`) | `GameConfig.appRules` stores only changed apps; `ruleFor(pkg)` defaults to `LetUsDecide` |
| Always important | Classified Important (`app_always_important`), outcome `Bypass`; no roll, no damage |
| Always bait | Classified Bait (`app_always_bait`); no AI call and no probability roll, an eligible tap is always caught |
| Let us decide | Follows the AI verdict in `NotificationContext.judged`: Important (`ai_important`) bypasses; Bait (`ai_bait`) rolls against the catch probability |
| No AI result | Unknown, outcome `NoPenalty`, no roll. Reasons include `ai_not_configured`, `ai_pending`, `ai_pending_timeout`, `ai_request_failed`, `ai_unsure` |
| Freshness | `freshnessSeconds` 600 (0 = off, max 86400). A known age strictly greater than the window is Unknown `stale`: no classification, no roll, no timer reset. Age is `ageMillis` (since the latest update), or `firstSeenAgeMillis` when `freshnessFromFirstSeen` is on (falls back to `ageMillis` if unknown). Unknown ages are never stale. Settings choices: 5, 10, 15, 30, 60 minutes; re-enabling restores 600 s |
| Lockout | 15 s after a catch (`lockoutSeconds`, 1-3600). Bait taps during it are `NoPenalty` `lockout`: no roll, no damage, no extension |
| Recovery | +5 health (`recoveryPerHour`, 0-100, the amount per interval) every 60 minutes (`recoveryIntervalMinutes`, 1-1440). Partial intervals carry over; health is not banked above 100 |
| Recovery timer reset | Only a catch resets it. A missed roll (`roll_passed`), stale, Unknown or Important taps keep partial progress |
| Recovery timing | Settled lazily on every operation and on `refresh()`, including offline time. `GameRepository` schedules its own refresh at `GameEngine.nextScheduledChangeMillis()` (next recovery step or end of a timed disable) |
| Death (health 0) | No recovery until `reset()`. Every Bait tap is caught without a roll (100%), with no further damage, and still starts the lockout and the pending choice |
| Reset | Only allowed when dead: health 100, clears lockout and pending catch, restarts recovery; keeps settings, history and counters |
| Pending catch | Every catch (tap or forced) records one `PendingCatch`: id `"<now>-<totalCatches>"`, package, health before/after, classifier rule, channel name. Its continue penalty is `min(CONTINUE_EXTRA_DAMAGE = 5, health after the catch)` |
| Catch choice | `settleCatchChoice(id, continueOriginalApp)`: "Go to original app" subtracts the saved continue penalty (health record `continue_after_catch`); "Go to Taptation" costs nothing. Either way the pending catch is cleared. The catch damage itself is never applied again. A new catch while a choice is still pending (e.g. after the in-app dialog was dismissed) supersedes it: the old one is treated as "Go to Taptation" (no continue penalty) and only the newest is offered |
| Disabled game | `active = false` (optionally until `disabledUntilMillis`). Taps return `NoPenalty` `disabled` and are not recorded in stats; dismissals are ignored; recovery stops; disabling clears any pending catch. A timed disable re-activates itself when it ends |
| Disable gate (`DisableGate`) | `beginDisable()` returns a single-use challenge; `confirmDisable(id, minutes)` succeeds only after a 10 s monotonic wait (`SystemClock.elapsedRealtime`). Durations: 15, 60 or null (until re-enabled). `enable()` is immediate and cancels any challenge. `updateConfig` refuses to change activation directly |
| Clock | Wall-clock timestamps; the engine never moves its observed time backward, so a backward clock change cannot award recovery or shorten a lockout. A forward change can. Not tamper-resistant |
| History | Latest 1,000 tap records and 1,000 health records; `tapsPerApp` and `totalCatches` stay cumulative |

Tap outcomes (`TapOutcome`): `Bypass` (Important), `NoPenalty` (Unknown, stale, disabled,
lockout, missed roll), `Caught` (damage already applied). `TapRecord.reason` is the final decision
(`caught`, `roll_passed`, `lockout`, or the classifier reason for Important/Unknown);
`TapRecord.rule` is the classifier rule behind the classification.

Order inside `GameEngine.onTap`: settle recovery -> disabled check -> `NotificationClassifier.assessTap`
(stale check, then `assess`) -> Important/Unknown stop here -> lockout -> dead, Always bait, or
`random() < probability` -> catch; otherwise `roll_passed`.

### AI verdict (Let us decide)

`JudgeQueue` judges countable "Let us decide" notifications when they are posted (memory only, by
key). On a tap, `TapListenerService` calls `JudgeQueue.contextForTap`, which uses a finished verdict
or waits up to `TAP_GRACE_MILLIS` (1 s) for an in-flight one, then `ai_pending_timeout` (Unknown).
`ClefJudge` maps the model's bait probability with strictness thresholds Relaxed 0.85, Balanced 0.7
(default), Strict 0.55: at or above the threshold is Bait, below is Important. A notification with
no title and no text is Bait (`ai_missing_content`) without a model call. Without Cloudflare keys,
every Let us decide tap is Unknown (`ai_not_configured`).

### Debug-only overrides

Honoured only in debuggable builds (`GameEngine(allowDebugOverrides)`, `GameRepository` `check(debug)`):

- `debugCatchProbability` (any value 0.0-1.0) replaces the difficulty probability. `setDifficulty`
  clears it. A release engine ignores a stored value.
- `debugRecoveryIntervalMinutes`: 1, 5 or 15 minutes instead of 60.
- `setHealthForDebug`, `advanceTimeForDebug(minutes)`, `resetDemoDataForDebug`, and forced
  catches through `applyCatch(level)` (debug panel).

`GameRepository.updateConfig` strips both debug fields in release builds; add any new debug field
there too.

### Legacy rule classifier

`NotificationClassifier.assessByRules` (whitelist, call/alarm/reminder/event categories, VIP names,
important keywords `urgent`, `code`, `meeting invite`, `meeting invitation`, channel rules, app
profiles Outlook/Instagram/Discord, bait packages/keywords/app categories) is **legacy and off the tap
path**. The matching `GameConfig` fields are still stored for compatibility. Taps and dismissals
use `assessTap` / `assess` only.

## Listener -> logic contract

`TaptationApplication.onCreate` installs the single `GameRepository` as `TapDispatcher.handler`, so
it works when only the listener process starts.

```kotlin
TapDispatcher.dispatch(context: NotificationContext)   // tap (REASON_CLICK)
TapDispatcher.dispatchDismiss(context)                  // swipe / clear-all, stats only
TapDispatcher.dispatch(packageName)                     // legacy, package only
TapDispatcher.dispatch(packageName, ageMillis)          // legacy, CompletableFuture<TapResult>
```

- `TapHandler` also has `onNotificationPosted(context)`, `onNotificationRemoved(key)` and
  `onListenerReset()`; the repository keeps a 500-entry context cache for the legacy
  `(packageName, ageMillis)` call, which uses cached metadata only when exactly one notification of
  that package is cached (otherwise package-only, so a Let us decide tap is Unknown).
- Callbacks arrive on the main thread; `GameRepository` does all work on one worker thread and
  resolves `ApplicationInfo.category` there.
- Dismissals are classified with `assessTap` (no roll) and recorded in stats; they never change
  health.
- Title and text are transient: never persisted or logged.

## Backend API for the UI

The UI reads and calls the backend through `(context.applicationContext as TaptationApplication)`.
The full list, including `feedback`, `rulePicker`, `apps`, `system`, `stats` and `meadow`, is in
[ui-backend-contract.md](../ui-backend-contract.md). Game-related parts of `game: GameRepository`:

| API | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `state: StateFlow<GameState?>` | Snapshot; null while loading or after an initialization failure |
| `error: StateFlow<String?>` | Latest operation failure |
| `lastResult: StateFlow<TapResult?>` | Latest tap result, for diagnostics; not an event queue |
| `refresh()` | Settle recovery (also called by `TaptationApplication` on every activity resume) |
| `setDifficulty(d)` | Also clears the debug catch probability |
| `setFreshnessEnabled(b)`, `setFreshnessMinutes(m)`, `setFreshnessFromFirstSeen(b)` | Minutes must be in `GameConfig.FRESHNESS_CHOICES_MINUTES` |
| `setCriteria(essential, nonEssential)`, `setStrictness(s)` | Let us decide answers (each cut to 1,000 chars) and strictness |
| `setAppRule(pkg, rule)`, `clearAppRule(pkg)`, `markAppImportant(pkg)` | Per-app rules; `LetUsDecide` removes the entry. `setWhitelisted` is a legacy alias |
| `beginDisable()`, `confirmDisable(id, minutes)`, `cancelDisable()`, `enable()`, `disableWaitRemainingMillis(challenge)` | Pause flow through `DisableGate` |
| `settleCatchChoice(id, continueOriginalApp)`, `dismissCatch(id)` | Used by `CatchFeedback`; screens go through `feedback.actionsFor(id)` |
| `reset()` | Only when dead |
| `recoveryIntervalMinutes(config)` | Interval in force (debug override only in debug builds) |
| `updateConfig { ... }` | Debug panels only; screens use the typed actions |

All mutations return `CompletableFuture` completed on the worker; never `.get()` / `.join()` on the
UI thread. Observe `state` instead.

Catch presentation (`service/CatchFeedback`): turns `state.pendingCatch` into
`feedback.prompt: StateFlow<CatchPrompt?>` (app label, `CatchDetails` from the pending catch,
continue penalty, `postponed`, `animate` on first showing). In the background it shows the overlay
(`CatchSurface`) when overlay permission is granted, otherwise a notification; in the foreground the
app shows a dialog. Both surfaces offer only the two destinations. Actions: `choose(ourApp)`,
`postpone()` (dismissing the in-app dialog), `feedback.resume(id)` ("Choose now"), and `correct()`
(opens Taptation with a `CorrectionRequest`; no caught button calls it since the "This should be
important" button was removed).

**Do not call `applyCatch` in response to `Caught`: the damage is already applied.** Render the
lockout from `lockoutUntilMillis` and the current time.

## Storage

- **Game state:** private SharedPreferences `taptation_game`, key `snapshot`, one Base64 binary
  snapshot written atomically with `commit()` on the worker (`PreferencesGameStore`,
  `GameStateCodec`). Current version **v9** (same fields as v8; v8 added the pending catch's health
  before/after, rule and channel). Only snapshots before v9 normalize the old defaults on load
  (lockout 30 s -> 15 s, Savage damage 35 -> 10); from v9 those values are kept as chosen. Reads v1-v9; v6 exists in three layouts (`V6_RULES`, `V6_PENALTY`, `V6_MERGED`), all
  tried on load. Pre-v6 `whitelistedPackages` / `baitPackages` migrate to `appRules`; old free
  probabilities map to the nearest difficulty.
- **Layout rule:** never reuse a version number across branches. Bump the version, add a
  `GameStateCodec.Layout`, and test old snapshots with `GameStateCodec.encode(state, Layout.X)`.
- **Unreadable snapshot:** kept under `snapshot_unreadable`, and a fresh game starts.
- A failed save throws and the new state is not published. Queued work is not durable until its save
  completes.
- **Stats:** `SqliteStatsStore`, database `stats.db`, schema version 2 (v2 added the category
  column), one row per tap or dismissal with classification, caught flag, age and notification
  category. See [decision-stats-handler.md](../decision-stats-handler.md).

## Verification

`GameEngine` takes an injected clock and random source, so JVM tests fast-forward time and force
rolls:

```powershell
.\gradlew.bat testDebugUnitTest
```

On-device steps (debug catch chance, test notifications, stale taps, both catch destinations) are in
[debug-controls-and-testing.md](../debug-controls-and-testing.md).
